card.name: Asma kasma
card.era: One of the oldest Azerbaijani dances
card.tagline: A slow, leaping wedding dance escorting the bride
card.profile: Asma Kasma (Azerbaijani: Asma Kəsmə, "hanging cutting") is described as one of the oldest Azerbaijani dances, performed at weddings: it accompanies the escorting of the bride to the bridegroom's home, with women dancing opposite the bride. Its tempo is slow and slightly exaggerated and the dance is full of jumps (Azerbaijani dances / en-academic; AzerNews). It takes its name from the music called "Asma-Kasma."
card.insight: As a dedicated bridal-procession dance, asma kasma is part of the ceremonial (wedding) category of Azerbaijani folk dance, marking the bride's transition between households in a tradition reaching back to the early Middle Ages (Azerbaijani dances).
